Facor Alloys Ltd presents a precarious financial profile defined by severe operational decay and structural instability. The company has suffered a catastrophic 83% decline in compounded sales growth over the last three years [E15], while operating margins have collapsed to -752% in the trailing twelve months [E27]. This deterioration is compounded by a critical liquidity risk, as the current ratio of 0.50x indicates that current liabilities significantly exceed current assets [E35]. Furthermore, the company’s inability to generate shareholder value is evidenced by a negative return on equity of -18.2% [E12] and a negative ROCE of -17.6% [E11]. The risk to shareholders is exacerbated by the fact that promoters have pledged 70.9% of their holdings [E51], and the company is burdened by high debtors of 7,377 days [E52]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10x [E34] and trades at a discount to book value [E1], which some may interpret as a margin of safety [E42]. However, these metrics fail to offset the fundamental erosion of the business model and the alarming lack of operational efficiency.
